concepts: locating Satpura range on outline map
questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the Satpura.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Satpura range: a chain of hills running EAST-WEST in central India, south of the Narmada river (the Vindhyas lie north of it). It runs from the Rajpipla hills in Gujarat through Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra to the Maikal range and Amarkantak (Chhattisgarh), roughly 21-23 deg N. Mark it as a hill band south of the Narmada and label 'Satpura'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the Gulf of Kutch.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Gulf of Kutch: an inlet of the Arabian Sea on the west coast of Gujarat, between the Kutch peninsula (north) and the Kathiawar (Saurashtra) peninsula (south). Shade the water inlet and label it.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the River Chambal.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). River Chambal: rises near Mhow (Janapao hills) in Madhya Pradesh, flows north-north-east through Rajasthan (past Kota) and joins the Yamuna in Uttar Pradesh near Etawah. Draw this line and label 'Chambal'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label Delhi.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Delhi: about 28.6 deg N, 77.2 deg E, in north India on the river Yamuna, at the northern end of the Aravalli range. Mark a dot and label 'Delhi'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label 80°30' E longitude.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). 80 deg 30' E: a north-south line (meridian) in the east-central part of the map. It lies just EAST of Chennai (80 deg 17' E) and Kanpur (80 deg 21' E) and just WEST of Lucknow (80 deg 56' E); it passes through Uttar Pradesh, the Telangana/Andhra Pradesh region and meets the Bay of Bengal coast near the Krishna delta. Draw the line from top to bottom and label it '80 deg 30' E'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label Jharia coalfield.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Jharia coalfield: Dhanbad district, Jharkhand, eastern India, on the Damodar river valley (about 23.7 deg N, 86.4 deg E). Mark a dot and label 'Jharia'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark with arrows and name the Southwest Monsoon winds.

South-West Monsoon winds: arrows starting from the Arabian Sea / Indian Ocean in the south-west and pointing north-east towards the west coast (Western Ghats), and from the Bay of Bengal pointing north-west along the Ganga plain. Draw arrows and label 'SW Monsoon'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

questions.question: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the Karakoram Pass.
questions.solution: Model answer (the board paper prints no key for map-marking items; written from standard geography references). Karakoram Pass: Ladakh, in the extreme north (about 35.5 deg N, 77.8 deg E), on the India-China border north of Leh. Mark a dot at the top of the map and label 'Karakoram Pass'.
questions.figure_desc: Outline map of India provided with the paper; student marks the feature on it.

concepts: four seasons of India and months
questions.question: Name the seasons of India and mention the durations of each season.
questions.solution: Four seasons: (a) Cold Weather (Winter) Season: December to February; (b) Hot Weather (Summer) Season: March to May; (c) Rainy (Monsoon) Season: June to September; (d) Retreating Monsoon Season: October to November.

marking_points.point: Cold weather/winter season: December to February
Hot weather/summer season: March to May
Rainy/monsoon season: June to September
Retreating monsoon season: October to November

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why does maximum rainfall in India occur after the summer season?
questions.solution: The Southwest monsoon winds bring maximum rainfall in India. Due to differential heating and cooling of land and sea, low pressure develops over the land in summer while pressure over the Indian Ocean is high; moisture-laden winds from the ocean blow towards the land and bring heavy rain at the end of summer.

marking_points.point: Differential heating of land and sea: land heats up, creating low pressure over land / relatively high pressure over Indian Ocean
Moisture-laden southwest monsoon winds blow from the ocean to land and give heavy rain after summer

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
concepts: windward vs rain shadow: Malabar vs Coromandel
questions.question: Give a geographical reason: The Malabar coast receives heavy rainfall in the month of July but the Coromandel coast during this time remains comparatively dry.
questions.solution: The Malabar coast lies on the western coastal plain where the Southwest Monsoon strikes first (windward side), so it gets heavy rain. The Coromandel coast on the eastern coastal plain lies in the rain-shadow region of the Western Ghats and gets less rain in July (its rain comes from the North East monsoon).

marking_points.point: Malabar coast is on the windward side facing the SW monsoon, so it gets heavy rain
Coromandel coast is in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats / gets rain mainly from the NE monsoon, so it is dry in July

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a geographical reason: Punjab receives rainfall in winter season.
questions.solution: Punjab gets rainfall in winter due to western disturbances. This rainfall is beneficial for rabi crops such as wheat and barley.

marking_points.point: Western disturbances bring winter rainfall to Punjab

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
concepts: maritime vs continental climate: Mumbai vs Delhi
questions.question: Give a geographical reason: Mumbai is warmer than Delhi in the month of December.
questions.solution: Mumbai is located on the shore of the sea, so it has a maritime (equable) climate; the large amount of water keeps the climate warmer in winter and cooler in summer. Delhi, far inland, has a continental climate with cold winters.

marking_points.point: Mumbai's coastal location/sea influence gives moderate, warmer winters (Delhi is inland/continental)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a geographical reason: Terrace farming is an ideal soil conservation method for hilly areas.
questions.solution: The hill slope is cut into a series of terraces giving enough level land for cultivation. This checks the flow of water, promotes absorption of water by the soil and thus reduces erosion.

marking_points.point: Slopes cut into terraces, giving level land for cultivation

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a geographical reason: Khadar soils are preferred over Bhangar soils.
questions.solution: Khadar soils consist of fine silt and clay and are very fertile as they are replenished every year by floods; Bhangar soils contain pebbles and gravel and are coarse.

marking_points.point: Khadar is fine silt/clay, replenished yearly by floods, very fertile
Bhangar is coarse with pebbles/gravel, less fertile

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Give a geographical reason: Foothills of Himalayas have been affected by soil erosion.
questions.solution: The foothills have little vegetation cover; there are not many plant or tree roots to hold the soil in place, leading to excessive soil erosion.

marking_points.point: Little vegetation cover on the foothills
Few roots to bind soil, so excessive erosion

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Distinguish between inundation canal and perennial canal.
questions.solution: Inundation canals have water only when excess water flows into them during the rainy season (river floods); perennial canals have water throughout the year as they draw water from perennial sources such as reservoirs and rivers.

marking_points.point: Inundation canals carry water only in the rainy season/flood time
Perennial canals carry water throughout the year from perennial sources

Port facility for import of raw cotton/machinery and export of cloth

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why are the petrochemical products in great demand?
questions.solution: They are cost effective, economic and cheap; raw materials are easily available.

marking_points.point: Cheap/cost effective
Raw materials easily available (or another valid reason)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention two problems faced by the sugar industry of India.
questions.solution: The price of sugarcane is fixed by the government, so farmers are dissatisfied; the industry is seasonal as sugarcane is available only at harvest and the crushing season is short, so cost of production is high.

marking_points.point: Government-fixed cane price / farmers' dissatisfaction (or other valid problem)
Seasonal industry, short crushing season, high cost (or other valid problem)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Where is Tata Steel located?
questions.solution: Tata Iron and Steel Company is located at Tatanagar near Jamshedpur in Jharkhand.

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why is the Silk industry losing the market in recent times?
questions.solution: Because of competition from artificial and synthetic fibres.

marking_points.point: Competition from artificial/synthetic fibres

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why is it important to have a well developed means of transport in India?
questions.solution: An efficient transport system provides basic strength to the national economy and links production and consumption of goods; growth of transport accelerates industrialisation and urbanisation.

marking_points.point: Strengthens economy / link between production and consumption
Accelerates industrialisation and urbanisation (or other valid point)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: "Though an expensive mode of transport, Airways is gaining popularity in India." Explain giving two reasons.
questions.solution: It is the fastest and most comfortable mode of transport; it can cover difficult terrain such as mountains, deserts, forests and oceans with ease.

marking_points.point: Fastest/most comfortable mode
Can cover difficult terrain (mountains, deserts, forests, oceans)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why are South Indian rivers not ideal for inland water transport?
questions.solution: Most peninsular rivers are seasonal and dry up in summer.

marking_points.point: Peninsular rivers are seasonal / dry up in summer

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention two advantages of waterways.
questions.solution: They are the cheapest means of transport for heavy and bulky goods; they are fuel efficient and environment friendly.

marking_points.point: Cheapest for heavy/bulky goods
Fuel efficient / environment friendly

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why are roadways considered more important than any other means of transport?
questions.solution: Roads are comparatively easier and cheaper to construct and maintain; they can negotiate steep slopes and sharp turns and provide door-to-door service.

marking_points.point: Easier and cheaper to build and maintain
Negotiate slopes/turns and give door-to-door service

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention two advantages of using railways as means of transport.
questions.solution: Railways have helped in developing tourism; they are the main mode of transport for freight and passengers.

marking_points.point: Helped develop tourism (or other valid advantage)
Main mode for freight and passengers (or other valid advantage)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Why should waste management be practiced in every school?
questions.solution: Applying the 3Rs (reduce, reuse, recycle): reducing means lessening the trash produced and reusing paper; reducing, reusing and recycling waste improves the economic and environmental performance of the school.

marking_points.point: Applying 3Rs (reduce, reuse, recycle) lessens waste produced
Improves the school's economic and environmental performance

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
concepts: dumping of waste pros and cons
questions.question: Mention one advantage and one disadvantage of dumping of waste.
questions.solution: Advantage: it is the conventional, inexpensive and widely used method of waste disposal. Disadvantage: solid waste left in the open gives out bad odour and is a breeding ground for mosquitoes, flies and harmful bacteria that cause diseases.

marking_points.point: Advantage: inexpensive / widely used
Disadvantage: bad odour / breeding ground for mosquitoes, flies, bacteria and disease

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: How is segregation of the waste helpful?
questions.solution: Segregation is the first and important step of safe disposal for effective waste management; it causes lesser pollution.

marking_points.point: First step of safe disposal / makes effective management possible / lesser pollution

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention one way in which we can reuse waste.
questions.solution: Old tyres can be reused for making shoes, chappals, etc.

marking_points.point: Any valid way of reusing waste (e.g. old tyres into chappals)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention one benefit of Composting.
questions.solution: Compost is a way of recycling and reusing organic waste; it reduces waste accumulation and increases plant growth.

marking_points.point: Reduces waste / increases plant growth (any valid benefit)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: How is recycling of waste helpful? Give an example of recycling of waste.
questions.solution: Recycling reduces the consumption of raw materials and energy and reduces air and water pollution. Example: paper is recycled so fewer trees are cut, saving forests.

marking_points.point: Reduces use of raw materials/energy and pollution
Valid example of recycling (e.g. paper)

questions.choice_note: any 5 of 9 questions in Part II
questions.question: Mention any one initiative taken by the Government to manage waste.
questions.solution: Swachh Bharat Mission (also National Water Mission, Waste to Wealth Mission).

marking_points.point: Names a valid initiative, e.g. Swachh Bharat Mission
